questionText: What toxic chemical contaminations have emerged in Indian groundwater due to severe over-extraction?

options.text: Groundwater is contaminated with molten gold in Kerala
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: All groundwater has turned into liquid petroleum
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Excessive pumping of groundwater has lowered water tables, concentrating fluoride in Rajasthan/Gujarat and arsenic in West Bengal/Bihar
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Water Quality Problems.

options.text: Excessive rain has dissolved platinum into Himalayan streams
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Water Quality Problems (India: Resources and Development):
Over-withdrawal of groundwater in parts of Rajasthan and Gujarat has led to high concentrations of fluoride, while over-extraction in the alluvial aquifers of West Bengal and Bihar has caused lethal arsenic contamination.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
